q: Section 2 of RA 11036 expressly recognizes that which existing law applies to persons with mental health conditions?
options: The Magna Carta for Disabled Persons (RA 7277)
explain: Section 2 states that the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons, as amended, applies to persons with mental health conditions as defined in the Act.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the objectives listed in Section 3?
options: Strengthen leadership and governance for mental health
Integrate mental health care in basic health services
Replace PhilHealth with a separate mental health insurance system
Strengthen information systems, evidence and research
explain: The six objectives cover governance, an integrated care system, rights, information and research, integration in basic services, and promotion in schools, workplaces and communities. Replacing PhilHealth is not among them.

q: Within how many hours of admission to a mental health facility must a service user be told of their rights?
explain: Section 5 gives service users the right to be informed of their rights within twenty-four hours of admission, in a form and language they understand.

q: Which is NOT one of the exceptions that allow disclosure of a service user's records without written consent?
options: Disclosure required by law or a court order
A life-threatening emergency where disclosure is needed to prevent harm
A request from the service user's employer
A minor believed by the attending professional to be a victim of child abuse
explain: Section 5(l) lists five exceptions: law or court order, the user's consent, a life-threatening emergency, a minor believed to be an abuse victim, and a case against a mental health professional. An employer's request is not one.

q: Under Section 5, if a service user cannot afford a lawyer, which body shall assist them?
options: The Public Attorney's Office or a legal aid institution
explain: Section 5(q) provides legal services through counsel of the user's choice, and the Public Attorney's Office or a legal aid institution assists if the user cannot afford counsel.

q: What form of consent does Section 8 require before a treatment or therapy plan, including restraint, is carried out?
options: Verbal consent recorded by a nurse
Consent from the family, not the user
explain: Section 8 requires service users to provide informed consent in writing before any plan or program of therapy or treatment, including physical or chemical restraint.

q: Who does Section 8 presume to possess legal capacity?
options: All persons, including service users, persons with disabilities and minors, regardless of their condition
Only those assessed by a professional
Only those who have a legal representative
explain: Everyone is presumed to have legal capacity for the purposes of the Act irrespective of the nature or effects of a mental health condition or disability.

q: What formalities does Section 9 require for an advance directive?
options: Signed and witnessed by a relative
Approved by the internal review board
explain: An advance directive must be signed, dated and notarized, and can be revoked by a new directive or a notarized revocation.

q: A service user has not appointed a legal representative. Under Section 10, who acts first (unless separated by decree or abandonment)?
options: A person appointed by a court
explain: The order is: the spouse, non-minor children, either parent by mutual consent if the user is a minor, the chief, administrator or medical director of the facility, then a court-appointed person.

q: How many supporters may a service user designate for supported decision making under Section 11?
explain: A service user may designate up to three supporters, including the legal representative.

q: Which of these is named in Section 12 as a member of a facility's internal review board?
options: A representative of the Department of Health
explain: The board includes a DOH representative, a CHR representative, a nominee of an accredited service-user or family organization, and other members set by the implementing rules.

q: When involuntary treatment or restraint is ordered during an emergency, within how many days must the internal review board review the order?
explain: Section 13(c) requires review by the internal review board within 15 days of the order and every 15 days thereafter while the treatment or restraint continues.

q: In an emergency, treatment without consent must comply with the service user's advance directive, if one exists, unless:
options: Doing so would pose an immediate risk of serious harm to the patient or another person
The facility is short of staff
The directive is more than a year old
explain: Section 13(a) makes the advance directive binding except where following it would pose an immediate risk of serious harm.

q: Under Section 15, every LGU and academic institution must create its own mental health program following general guidelines set by:
options: The Philippine Council for Mental Health
The Department of the Interior and Local Government
explain: Section 15 directs LGUs and academic institutions to follow general guidelines set by the Philippine Council for Mental Health.

q: Who funds the establishment of community-based mental health care facilities under Section 16?
options: The national government through the DOH
explain: The national government, through the DOH, funds their establishment and assists in their operation in provinces, cities and clusters of municipalities.

q: How often must LGUs report to the Philippine Council for Mental Health through the DOH (Section 17)?
explain: LGUs, through their health offices, make a quarterly report, without disclosing the identities of service users.

q: Section 18 requires which hospitals, including private ones serving paying patients, to provide a set of psychiatric and neurologic services?
options: Only hospitals with a psychiatry department
explain: All regional, provincial and tertiary hospitals, including private hospitals rendering service to paying patients, must provide services such as short-term inpatient care, partial hospital care, outpatient care, home care and a referral system.

q: What does Section 21 say about hotlines?
options: 24/7 hotlines are to be set up and existing ones strengthened
Hotlines are limited to office hours
Only private groups may run hotlines
explain: Section 21 requires suicide intervention, prevention and response mechanisms, with attention to young people, and 24/7 hotlines.

q: Section 24 requires all public and private educational institutions to have:
options: A complement of mental health professionals
explain: Educational institutions develop mental health policies and programs, and all public and private institutions are required to have a complement of mental health professionals.

q: What was the National Center for Mental Health formerly called, according to Section 29?
explain: Section 29 names the NCMH, formerly the National Mental Hospital, the premier training and research center for mental and neurological service interventions.

q: Under Section 30, the DOH coordinates with PhilHealth so that insurance packages for mental health conditions are:
options: Equivalent to those covering physical disorders of comparable impact
explain: Section 30(f) directs the DOH to coordinate with PhilHealth to ensure equivalent insurance packages, measured by disability-adjusted life years or other methods.

q: Which is a duty of LGUs under Section 37?
options: Passing a local ordinance on mental health consistent with national policy
Chairing the Philippine Council for Mental Health
explain: LGUs formulate local regulations and guidelines, including a local ordinance on mental health, integrate mental health into basic health care, train providers, promote deinstitutionalization and more.

q: Who chairs the Philippine Council for Mental Health (Section 41)?
explain: The Secretary of Health is chairperson. Other government members include the Secretaries of Education, Labor and the Interior and Local Government, and the CHR and CHED chairpersons.

q: The DOH Mental Health Division created by Section 42 sits under which bureau?
explain: The division is under the Disease Prevention and Control Bureau, implements the National Mental Health Program and serves as the Council's secretariat.

q: Which penalty does Section 44 set for violations such as failing to obtain informed consent or breaching confidentiality?
options: Imprisonment of six months to two years, a fine of P10,000 to P200,000, or both
A fine only, up to P5,000
Revocation of the facility's license only
Imprisonment of five to ten years
explain: Four acts are punishable: failure to secure informed consent, breach of confidentiality, discrimination and inhumane or unscientific treatment.

q: Within how many days of the Act's effectivity was the Secretary of Health to issue the implementing rules (Section 46)?
explain: The Secretary of Health, in coordination with other agencies and service-user and professional groups, issues the rules within one hundred twenty days.

q: Which earlier DOH orders did AO 2016-0039 repeal?
explain: The repealing clause repeals the operational framework for a sustainable mental health program, AO 2007-0009 and 2007-0009A. AO 8 s. 2001, the 2001 National Mental Health Policy, is acknowledged but not repealed.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the five components of the National Mental Health Program in AO 2016-0039?
explain: The five components are Wellness of Daily Living, Extreme Life Experience, Mental Disorders, Neurologic Disorders, and Substance Abuse and Other Forms of Addiction.

q: Which set lists the three strategic approaches of the Action Framework?
explain: The program is anchored on a health systems approach, a whole-of-government approach and a whole-of-society approach.

q: Which DOH body chairs the Technical Working Group for the National Mental Health Program?
explain: The Technical Working Group is chaired by the Disease Prevention and Control Bureau, whose Essential Non-Communicable Disease Division serves as secretariat.

q: Who chairs the Oversight Committee that advises the Secretary of Health?
options: The Undersecretary or Assistant Secretary of Health for Technical Services
The Chair of the League of Mayors
explain: The Oversight Committee is chaired by the Undersecretary or Assistant Secretary of Health, Office for Technical Services, and reviews the Technical Working Group's outputs.

q: In AO 2016-0039, which body develops and implements health insurance packages for people at risk of or living with MNS disorders?
options: The Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau
explain: Part X assigns PhilHealth to guide information needs and to develop and implement insurance packages covering identification, assessment, diagnosis, management, rehabilitation and support services.

q: Which DOH bureau leads coordination of mental health and psychosocial support in disasters, epidemics and humanitarian emergencies?
options: Knowledge Management and Information Technology Service
Health Policy Development and Planning Bureau
explain: The Health Emergency Management Bureau leads on assessing MNS needs and providing MHPSS in emergency settings.

q: Which unit regularly reviews and updates the essential medicines list for MNS disorders?
options: The Pharmaceutical Division of the Health Policy Development and Planning Bureau
The National Center for Mental Health
explain: The Pharmaceutical Division develops supply chain guidelines for affordable, quality medicines and keeps the essential medicines list for MNS disorders up to date.

q: Which role does AO 2016-0039 give to DOH regional offices?
options: Lead and give technical assistance to LGUs and regional hospitals, including on community-based services
Run the annual Program Implementation Review
explain: Part X(N) gives regional offices this lead role. The annual Program Implementation Review belongs to the Disease Prevention and Control Bureau.

q: What does one general guideline of AO 2016-0039 direct the National Mental Health Program to advocate for?
options: National legislation guaranteeing the rights and freedoms of persons with MNS disorders
Mandatory treatment for all drug users
explain: Part VII(I) says the program shall advocate for such legislation, which became RA 11036 in 2018.

q: Which is a guiding principle in Part V of AO 2016-0039?
options: Universal health coverage without the risk of impoverishment
explain: The six principles are universal health coverage, human rights, life course, evidence-based practice, multisectoral approach and empowerment of persons with psychosocial disabilities.

q: Who does AO 2016-0039 say provides funds for technical assistance, monitoring and health promotion, and may augment LGU funds?
options: The Disease Prevention and Control Bureau and DOH regional offices
explain: Part XI says LGUs, other agencies and civil society groups are encouraged to provide counterpart funds.

q: How does AO 2025-0028 define community-based mental health (CBMH)?
options: Delivery of mental and neurological health services within a geographically defined community
explain: Part IV defines CBMH as delivery of mental and neurological health services within a geographically defined community. In this order, mental health also covers neurological conditions.

q: Who exercises overall leadership and coordination of CBMH implementation?
options: The DOH, through the PCMH, relevant bureaus and the CHDs
explain: Part VII(A) gives the DOH, through the Philippine Council for Mental Health, its bureaus and its Centers for Health Development, overall leadership and coordination.

q: Into which local plans must LGUs integrate their CBMH strategies?
options: The Local Investment Plan for Health and the Annual Operation Plan
The Barangay Peace and Order Plan
explain: LGUs, through their local mental health council or local health board, develop CBMH strategies based on local profiles and integrate them into the LIPH and Annual Operation Plan.

q: Before preparing a CBMH Action Plan, what must LGUs conduct?
explain: LGUs conduct situational analyses and resource mapping to find needs and assets, then prepare a CBMH Action Plan integrated into the LIPH, following the Annex D template.

q: Community health workers are trained under which framework?
options: The Magna Carta for Health Workers
explain: Part VII(C) says CBMH implementers capacitate community health workers and members of the community based on the DOH competency framework for mental, neurological and substance use conditions, with Annex E setting minimum service requirements.

q: In Annex E, which health worker delivers the advanced competency level, including management and treatment?
explain: Basic: BHWs, midwives, nurses, physicians and other stakeholders. Intermediate: nurses. Advanced: physicians.

q: Basic mental and neurological health services in primary care are to be delivered by providers trained in which program?
explain: The order specifies mhGAP-trained primary care providers for screening, assessment and management of common conditions, including psychoeducation, counseling, telemedicine, wellness programs and medication.

q: Referral to higher-level facilities, and back to the community, uses which existing arrangement?
options: The Barangay Health Station network only
A new mental health referral agency
explain: Part VII says to facilitate access to specialized services for people needing referral to higher levels, and referral back to the community, using the existing HCPN.

q: Essential mental and neurological medicines are provided through which program?
options: The Medicine Access Program for Mental Health
explain: The order provides essential medicines for people needing drug treatment through the Medicine Access Program for Mental Health, with supervision by trained providers.

q: Which are named as accessible crisis intervention services in the minimum community package?
options: MHPSS, crisis hotlines and centers, and mobile health teams
explain: The order lists accessible crisis intervention services such as Mental Health and Psychosocial Support, crisis hotlines and centers, and mobile health teams.

q: In which months are CHDs and MOH-BARMM to submit quarterly reports?
explain: Reports are due in the month after the end of each quarter, that is April, July, October and January, using the prescribed template.

q: What does the order require before program data are shared with a third party?
options: Nothing, if the data are anonymized
explain: Part VII(H) makes a Data Sharing Agreement mandatory, guaranteeing comparable protection to the Data Privacy Act rules. A template is Annex H.

q: What is the PCMH's CBMH-specific role under Part VIII?
options: Lead a biennial, multi-sectoral review of CBMH implementation
Run all barangay mental health clinics
explain: The PCMH leads a biennial multi-sectoral review, gives technical guidance, and cascades member agencies' roles.

q: How does AO 2025-0028 provide for funding?
options: It creates a dedicated national fund
All agencies allocate the funding needed, consistent with their mandates and normal accounting and auditing rules
Funding is left entirely to NGOs
explain: The order states no dedicated budget. This is a point to note when analyzing how it will be implemented.

q: Until patient data are fully integrated into the Mental Health Information System, where are they recorded?
options: In the existing Field Health Service Information System and National Mental Health Program reports
explain: The transitory clause requires recording in the existing information systems and under the National Mental Health Program's reporting mechanisms.

q: Which LGU role in AO 2025-0028 involves the Persons with Disability Affairs Office?
options: Data profiling and issuing PWD IDs to eligible service users
explain: LGUs ensure or coordinate with the PDAO for data profiling, PWD IDs for eligible service users and links to federations of persons with disabilities.

q: Which of the three instruments is a statute passed by Congress that sets criminal penalties?
explain: Only RA 11036 is a law. It sets imprisonment and fines in Section 44. The two administrative orders are DOH issuances.

q: Which instrument first called for national legislation on the rights of persons with MNS disorders?
explain: AO 2016-0039 says the program shall advocate for such legislation. RA 11036 followed in 2018.

q: Which instrument sets three tiers of community competency (basic, intermediate, advanced)?
explain: Annex E of AO 2025-0028 sets the three levels and links each to who delivers it and what services they provide.

q: Which instrument created the Philippine Council for Mental Health?
explain: Sections 39 to 41 of RA 11036 establish the Council, its duties and its composition. AO 2025-0028 gives it a biennial review role.

q: Which instrument directly assigns PhilHealth to develop and implement insurance packages for MNS disorders?
explain: AO 2016-0039 Part X(F) gives PhilHealth this role. RA 11036 Section 30(f) instead directs the DOH to coordinate with PhilHealth.

q: Who consolidates LGU reports into quarterly regional summaries for the DOH under AO 2025-0028?
options: The Philippine Council for Mental Health
explain: CHDs monitor and evaluate CBMH in coordination with LGUs, consolidate LGU reports and submit regional summaries quarterly. RA 11036 Section 17 separately has LGUs report quarterly to the Council through the DOH.
